column1:
The FOMC statement notes modest Q1 growth, robust job gains, and elevated inflation, but the April Beige Book and SLOOS tilt the outlook more cautious. Beige Book references indicate only a few districts reported growth, with many seeing little change in overall activity; consumer spending showed moderate price growth, and auto sales remained steady rather than accelerating. Credit dynamics were notably weaker: lending volumes and loan demand declined as higher rates bit, and banks tightened standards broadly (C&I, CRE, and consumer credit), echoing SLOOS reports of wider spreads, lower LTVs, and higher DSCRs amid funding-cost pressures and deposit outflows. This combination supports the Committee’s warning that tighter credit will weigh on activity and hiring, even as the banking system remains resilient, and suggests downside risks to growth with some moderation in price pressures.

Net effect: more negative than the FOMC’s mildly cautious tone.
